suggestions.assertion: The documentation output contains AT LEAST 6 distinct markdown files
suggestions.reason: The without-skill run accidentally satisfies this at the exact boundary (6 == 6). A threshold of 7 or 8 would better discriminate the skill's multi-phase workflow from a capable baseline that writes 6 conventional docs without prompting.

No assertion checks that the API_REFERENCE.md actually documents SlugError with its triggers — the without-skill run may cover it superficially. An assertion like 'the error documentation includes trigger conditions and example stack traces' would be harder to satisfy without dedicated error-focused authoring.

The architecture assertion is the most discriminating of the three — without-skill produces no architecture file at all, confirming this is a meaningful skill-gated behavior. Consider also checking that the architecture file references the module hierarchy (e.g., slugify_utils/core.py, slugify_utils/languages/) rather than just naming 'module structure' generically.

eval_feedback.overall: The architecture and error-reference assertions are strong discriminators — both cleanly FAIL without the skill. The 6-file threshold is too easily met by a competent baseline; raising it would improve discrimination.
